reuse.why: All bulk actions use getBulkBudgetCategories, and the new action reuses averageToBudget, getSheetValue, setBudget, and the existing undo and mutation wrappers.

duplication.why: Category eligibility and amount sign handling remain shared without introducing duplicated decision logic.

placement.why: Budget policy stays in actions.ts, while handler registration and undo integration follow the established app.ts pattern.

scope.why: The changes address the requested actions and exclusions, although adding goal_def to getBudgetData retrieves an unused field.

maintainability.why: The centralized eligibility policy is straightforward to maintain, with minor unnecessary complexity in the new action's intermediate amounts array and redundant numeric normalization.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every affected bulk action, including setLastMonthSpending, calls getBulkBudgetCategories and retains shared sign conversion where applicable.

disguised_duplication.where: The diff extends the existing shared selector rather than reshaping eligibility logic into separate implementations.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories adds saved-template and #fixed exclusion branches; includeHidden is renamed to includeHiddenCategories without increasing the parameter count, and all bulk callers retain the shared selector.
